title: Harmonic Rollout Ledger — fractional rendezvous & emergency-shepherd plan
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for an alternative rollout pattern I want to try for multi-tenant model flips: a harmonic-fraction rendezvous schedule with a lightweight "shepherd" process for emergency steering.

High-level idea (one-liner):
Stagger cohorts using a harmonic fraction series (1/2, 1/3, 1/4...) to avoid simultaneous jumps, seed KV caches gradually, and maintain a thin ‘shepherd’ micro-runbook able to decant traffic to a safe variant within seconds.

Why this is different / rationale:
- Most ramps use fixed increments (1%, 5%, 10%, 25%) which concentrate traffic changes and cache pressure at predictable boundaries.
- Harmonic fractions distribute added load more smoothly across many small cohorts; early cohorts are larger so we get signal, later cohorts are smaller to avoid late spikes.
- Combine with tenant-tier awareness: apply larger fractions to high-volume tenants in early cohorts to detect pathologies quickly, then seed long tail tenants with tiny fractions.

Assumptions and constraints:
- We have per-tenant routing hooks and can route by header or tenant id.
- The runtime supports per-route model pinning TTL (suggested default 2h for initial ramp).
- Observability: p95/p99 latency, error rate, token throughput, model-side reject rate, and downstream client errors must be visible per tenant cohort in ~30s resolution.
- Warm cache helps: KV cache priming reduces latency spikes; plan includes passive priming for 10 minutes before each cohort is added.

Cohort algorithm (sketch):
1) Order tenants by 7-day qps decile (largest first).
2) For tenants in deciles 10-8 (top 30% traffic), schedule cohorts with fractions: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 (stops at cumulative ~0.9).
3) For deciles 7-4, use 1/5, 1/6, 1/7.
4) For deciles 3-1, use tiny rendezvous fractions: 1/20, 1/30, 1/50 (multiple passes).
5) For multi-tenant clients where we cannot partial funnel requests, fall back to per-client binary pin/unpin and use sticky SDK toggles.

Example schedule (top-line):
- T+0m: canary cohort A (50% of top tenants via rendezvous=1/2), passive priming 10m prior
- T+20m: cohort B (1/3 fraction of remaining top-tenants), observe 30m
- T+90m: cohort C (1/4 fraction), observe 60m
- After top-tier reaches steady-state, do a sweep of mid-tier with 1/5 then 1/6, etc.

Signal thresholds (quick reference):
- Latency: p95 increase > +25% from baseline for a cohort -> pause and investigate
- Error rate: absolute increase > 0.5% (or relative > 3x) -> revert cohort or divert
- Token throughput drop: sudden -30% for request success rate -> possible backpressure, investigate model OOMs
- Quality signal (if available): generation-perf regressions flagged by automated evals -> immediate pinback

Emergency shepherd (short runbook):
- Trigger sources: PagerDuty alert, Slack #infra-rollouts thread, manual from rollout owner.
- Automated first step: if latency or error threshold exceeded for a cohort for 3 consecutive 1m buckets, automatically divert that cohort to the previously pinned model variant (fallback).
- Manual steps: 1) Mark cohort paused in rollout dashboard; 2) Hotpatch routing rule to route cohort to fallback; 3) Notify teammates + CS for impacted customers with template message; 4) Start tracing golden requests (link to GitHub PR if repro); 5) Collect traces and spike logs (script: /ops/scripts/dump-cohort-traces.sh).

Version pinning notes (implementation constraints):
- Pin semantics: per-tenant HTTP header X-Redwood-Model-Pin TTL=7200s. Pin must be honored by SDK and edge routers.
- Default: automated pin on checkpoint (if flagged by automated rollback) lasts 24h unless manually cleared.
- For tenants with compliance flags, pin must be sticky until manual approval.

Warm cache & priming checklist (short):
- Warmup path: replay recent 1k prompts from that tenant in a private warmup queue (rate-limited at 10rps)
- Preflight: ensure KV cache is populated to expected median size for the model (script prints cache hit %).
- Observation window: 10m warm + 30m monitor after adding cohort.

Telemetry & dashboards to have ready before starting:
- Cohort-level p95/p99 latency sparkline, error-rate, 5-min request/second heatmap
- Cache hit ratio per model variant and cohort
- Model-side OOM/timeout counters and per-GPU queue length
- Synthetic golden prompt perf and hallucination QA checks (if enabled)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Q: Do rendezvous hashes create unfair grouping for some clients? Need a simulation on our tenant distribution.
- Q: Interaction with autoscaler: small steady ramps might keep autoscaler from scaling down — need cost sim.
- TODO: write a small playground script that simulates harmonic fractions across 10k tenants and plots request delta spikes. (assign to me)
- TODO: Draft a short runbook page in Confluence with the shepherd checklist and Slack alert templates.

Communication plan (one-paragraph):
- Short broadcast to #infra-rollouts at T-30m with expected cohorts and a link to the dashboard. Notify CS owners for top 50 tenants with a 1:1 note. If incident occurs, the shepherd will post every 5m status updates until stable. Postmortem to be owner-authored within 72 hours.

Rollback/decant scripts (practical):
- Quick commands (examples):
  - pinback: rcli routing set --cohort COHORT_ID --model fallback-v2 --reason "auto-shepherd"
  - snapshot cohort: rcli metrics export --cohort COHORT_ID --range 1h > /tmp/cohort-1234.json
  - unpin: rcli routing clear-pin --tenant TENANT_ID --force

Safety knobs I want to add to the dashboard (UX wishlist):
- One-click decant to fallback with automatic commit message and mandatory reason field
- Cohort age heatmap (how long each tenant has been on new model)
- Quick toggle to disable rendezvous for a tenant class

Notes-to-self closing:
- This will probably feel over-engineered for small flips but could materially reduce tail-chaos when we flip large models across thousands of tenants.
- Pilot idea: try harmonic schedule for a non-critical mid-sized model (experimental label) next week with Oliver as shepherd.

References and links (scratch):
- Related PR with preliminary hooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/421
- Simulation idea thread: #rollout-experiments on Slack (search terms: harmonic rendezvous)
- JIRA for follow ups: JIRA-8421

Unresolved: how to represent cohort identity in metrics without adding cardinality. Might need aggregated labels (cohort_bucket) and sampling.

End of scratchpad.
